nets: GPS RF / antenna node (U10.11 RF_IN – C66.2 – C67.1 – L2.2 – ANT1.1)
anomalies.observed: On the NAVC Peripherals sheet, in the 'GPS Receiver and SMA Antenna Connector' block, the shunt matching capacitor C67 at the u-blox MAX-8Q RF node is drawn with the value 10n (10 nF) to GND, in parallel with the 27 nH series inductor L2 and the 22 p series DC-block C66.
anomalies.expected: A GPS RF matching/bias shunt capacitor must be in the picofarad range (≈10 pF) so it presents a high impedance at the 1.575 GHz carrier; standard practice (and the role of this part as the shunt element of the L-match) requires ~10 pF, not 10 nF.

evidence.quote: NAVC Peripherals sheet, GPS block: 'C66 22p', 'L2 27n', 'C67 10n' (C67 tied from the RF/antenna node to GND)
GPS receiver | NAVCPeripherals | u-blox MAX-8Q ... (spec gives no RF-matching values; standard practice governs)

anomalies.impact: A 10 nF shunt at 1.575 GHz has an impedance of only ~0.01 Ω, shorting the GPS RF input to ground; the receiver would see no satellite signal and GPS fix would fail.

parsed.summary: The board otherwise matches the specification (correct FCC/NAVC parts, sensor set and addresses, power stage values, and the documented barometer RESET/EOC mix-up and MAX-8Q/MAX-7Q footprint note are reproduced as intended), but the GPS RF matching shunt capacitor C67 is drawn as 10 nF instead of the ~10 pF required, which would short the GPS RF input and prevent satellite reception.
